text: Kalila, if a giant snake stole your 3 eggs every spring, and you were just a tiny crow, how would you stop him?
Hmm. I would peck him on the nose! Peck, peck, peck!
Peck a giant snake? Ha! No, brother. Today's crow had a much smarter plan.
Once upon a time, two crows built a cozy nest, high up in a tall tree. Soon, there were three little eggs in it.
Look, my dear! Three eggs! Soon we will have three little babies!
But down at the bottom of the tree, in a dark hole, lived a big, greedy snake.
Hsss... Eggs! I smell eggs! Yummy eggs for my breakfast!
Every spring, the snake crept up the tree and stole the crows' eggs. And now, here he came again!
Go away, snake! Leave our eggs alone!
Hsss! You are too small to stop me. I will come back tomorrow!
Oh no! What can we do? He is so big, and we are so small.
Don't cry, my dear. Let's ask our friend, the wise old jackal. He always knows what to do.
So the father crow flew to the wise jackal and told him everything.
Hmm. Don't fight the snake with your little beak. Use your head instead!
Fly to the king's garden. Find something shiny, and make sure the guards see you take it. Then drop it into the snake's hole.
Into the snake's hole? Oh! I see! What a clever plan!
In the king's garden, the princess had left her shiny necklace on a stone, beside the pool.
Swoosh! Down flew the crow, and he picked it up with his beak.
Hey! That crow took the princess's necklace! After him!
The crow flew slowly, slowly, so the guards could follow him, all the way back to the tall tree.
This way! Follow me! Not too fast...
Then, plop! He dropped the necklace right into the snake's hole.
It fell in that hole! Let's get it out with my stick!
Hsss! Who is poking my house?
A snake! Shoo! Shoo! Go away, and never come back!
Hsss! Help! All right, all right, I'm going! I'm going!
And the snake slid away, far, far away, and he never came back. The guards took the necklace home to the princess.
And soon, crack, crack, crack! Three baby crows came out of their eggs.
Caw! Caw! Caw!
Thank you, wise jackal! A clever head is better than a big beak!
So the little crows could not fight the big snake. But they used their heads, and the bully had to go!
Cleverness beats a bully! And nobody got hurt at all.
Persian word of the day! In Persian, a snake is maar. Maar! Hsss!
Maar. A snake. But don't worry, our maar is gone for good.
And next time: a hungry heron, a clever crab, and a lake full of fish.
